messages:
incident-bot: pager: HIGH GPU_POOL_QUEUE_GROWTH on gpu-pool-us-east-1 (severity: P1). autoscaler failing to add capacity to pool 'inference-gpu-1' — queue length rising above 600. paging #oncall and #eng-runtime.

oncall-sre: ack. switching to incident mode. joining Zoom.

mona: seeing a lot of 429/503s from the hosted API, customers complaining about slow responses. logs show bursts for model=reddit-v4-optimized-v2.

priya: I can confirm autoscaler is hitting max_scale_limit for that pool (configured cap 48 GPUs). metrics: queued_requests=620, avg_latency_tokens=180ms, active_sessions=410.

sam: any recent deploys for that model?

mona: yes — rollout of reddit-v4-optimized-v2 started ~20m ago. Early metrics looked fine but kv-cache footprint started climbing around then.

neil: hypothesis: new attention caching changes in v2 increased per-session KV size, causing instances to run out of usable memory and reject new sessions -> queue piling up. checking instance OOM/eviction logs.

priya: here's the autoscaler event stream: ```
EVENT 2146001003 autoscaler: scale_request_to 52 rejected (cap 48)
EVENT 2146001030 node_pool: 3x pod_evictions due to gpu_mem_pressure
EVENT 2146001065 scale_backfill: attempted, no spare quota in region
```

oncall-sre: customers impacted: some PLG free-tier users hitting timeouts; 2 enterprise customers reported 5xx for 2+ minutes. CC @customer-success for outreach.

customer-success: alerted CSMs, opening tickets for affected customers A+ B. will send status update after mitigation.

sam: immediate mitigations we can try in parallel: 1) throttle new sessions to the pool, 2) route traffic to fallback model variant (v2-small-quant), 3) temporary increase cap with cloud vendor (if available), 4) rollback the v2 rollout.

neil: i'm pushing to enable per-route rate limits now to slow arrival rate into that pool. running: `redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --rate-limit 50rps --pool inference-gpu-1`

mona: applying fallback routing to the canary: `redwoodctl route set-fallback --route /v1/generate --model reddit-v4-optimized-v2-small` — will send 30% traffic to fallback.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: rollback reddit-v4-optimized-v2 -> reddit-v4-optimized-v1. initiating canary rollback to 10% now.

priya: vendor escalation: opened emergency quota request with cloud partner to raise GPU quota by 16 for us-east. ETA 18-40 minutes.

neil: noticed many long-living conversations holding large KV caches — adding TTL-based eviction to aggressive mode on pool to reclaim memory: `kvcache.eviction_policy=aggressive` applied. Expect partial relief in ~120s as old sessions free caches.

oncall-sre: monitoring queue size. before mitigations: queued=620. after rate-limit and fallback: queued=412 -> 260. good trend but still high.

mona: some pods still report tokenization/regression errors; digging into why v2-small isn't handling a few large-context requests. adding `max_context_tokens=4096` enforcement at ingress to avoid huge sessions hitting fallback.

sam: confirmed rollback to v1 at 10% -> metrics: per-session KV size dropped ~36%. queued_count dropping further.

customer-success: sent first customer update: "We're mitigating an infrastructure issue causing elevated errors for text generation. Root cause under investigation. Next update in 30m."

oncall-sre: can we get a rough ETA for full recovery if rollback continues vs vendor quota?

priya: prediction: if rollback completes to 100% and TTL eviction holds, queue likely back to acceptable (<50) in ~10-15 minutes. If we wait on vendor quota, could be 20-45m depending on approval and provisioning.

neil: started a warm-pool spin-up for smaller quantized instances to offload throughput: `infractl gpu-pool scale --pool inference-quant --count 12` — these use less memory and accept more sessions.

mona: observability note: added a temporary dashboard panel for 'per-session kvcache bytes' and 'queue length by route' so SRE and runtime can watch correlated metrics.

deploy-bot: rollback progressed to 60% at 2146001500. autoscaler still trimmed due to memory_evictions but overall load per pod down 28%.

oncall-sre: customer-impact update: 12 customers affected intermittently, 3 enterprise customers experienced sustained 5xx windows. No data loss. severity P1 continues.

sam: next steps: 1) finish rollback to 100% (in progress), 2) keep aggressive eviction enabled for 30m, 3) keep fallback routing to 10% for edge cases, 4) after stable, roll a patched model with reduced kv-cache allocation.

priya: vendor quota approved earlier than expected — +12 GPUs provisioned to us-east, started provisioning at 2146001660. however bring-up time ~12m. we can keep them as extra capacity buffer after recovery.

neil: logs show OOM evictions dropped to near-zero after rollback reached 95%, queued=48. nice.

oncall-sre: recommended immediate postmortem timeline: micro-postmortem in 48h, full incident review in one week. need owners: runtime (neil), autoscaler (priya), deploy (sam), customer comms (customer-success).

customer-success: will follow up with impacted customers after we confirm service stable. shared interim note: "We rolled back a recent model change that increased memory usage; we will deploy a fix and follow up."

mona: filing action item: runtime team to add pre-rollout KV usage smoke tests to CI, and add rollout guard to abort if median KV per-session grows >25% compared to baseline.

sam: adding a temporary safety valve: if any pool queue >300 for >2m, automatic partial rollback and traffic diversion to fallback model. creating ticket INF-4219.

neil: staying on the call until stable. nice work everyone.

oncall-sre: closing the paging loop: service considered recovered at 2146001745; last visible queue spike cleared. moving to follow-up mode. :tada:
__notes: Generated Slack-style incident thread about GPU pool exhaustion from model rollout. Single-thread string; messages prefixed by names. Metadata fields required by agents.md included.
